questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Power of a Nilpotent Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
Computing ${T}^{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{2} & =T\cdot T \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 \\ -12 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 \\ -12 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =O.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, since ${T}^{2}=O,$ the matrix $T$ is a nilpotent matrix of index $2.$ 

We can use this fact to compute ${T}^{6}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{6} & ={T}^{2}\cdot {T}^{4} \\  & =O\cdot {T}^{4} \\  & =O\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{T}^{6}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

$$
